concern_results.conclusion: Traced the prompt flow: non-neutral prompts advance the epoch first, then take the lock, then arm, suspend or revoke. Neutral prompts keep a target-goal grant only while its epoch matches. On the guard side, goal grants require the closed command grammar (exact family, id, repo, strategy, full SHA) plus a current epoch and the 60-minute limit. Suspended or malformed goal grants deny. Legacy one-shot and batch grants still clear on every new prompt.

No bypass found. The grammar rejects shell composition, API calls, --auto, --admin, unknown flags, duplicate --repo values and a mismatched repo or id. It checks the whole command against a restricted character set. Direct pushes to the default branch and auto-merge still deny before the release valve. Grant scope comes from local origin config and the user prompt, not from transcripts.

Lock timeout, a failed epoch write or a failed grant write all remove the grant or skip arming. A revoke that lands between mv and rearm is caught by the epoch checks after consume and the rearm is destroyed. If the epoch advances after the final check, the prompt still takes the lock and removes the rearmed sentinel. Origins with a port, embedded credentials or multiple lines stay unarmed.

The tests cover the full prompt-to-guard path: one-shot consume, the scope and grammar deny matrix, neutral preserve versus suspend, keeping the original expiry, rejecting a corrupted or missing epoch, two concurrent consumers and a forced revoke during consume. The 'git push origin main' deny row always leaves the grant intact because it denies before the grant is read, so it tests nothing about the grant; that isn't material. I didn't run the suites.

Grants written before the upgrade still work when neither epoch file exists; once epoch files exist, a missing or foreign one fails closed. Legacy grant formats are unchanged. The gh/glab family is chosen from the PR/MR word the user types, so a mismatch with the actual forge denies rather than allowing anything.
All state lives in per-uid temp files. Rolling back to the previous hook ignores JSON grants, which legacy parsing treats as having no grant and denies. No persistent migration risk.

Deny messages separate a missing, suspended or expired grant from a command that doesn't match the grammar, and say that no grant was consumed. The consume message states it covers only the current repo and PR/MR.

The docs and deny text correctly say the mechanism does not infer release goals or ownership of future PRs, and that a missing grant does not mean the user never authorized the goal. Runtime claims for native hosts are explicitly marked as not yet verified.

Each goal grant is tied to one repo and one PR/MR number, is used once, expires 60 minutes after arming and is re-checked against the epoch. Replay is prevented by the atomic mv plus the epoch checks. Unknown prompts suspend the grant and a neutral prompt cannot resume it. No escalation path found in the diff.

The change is to hook behavior, so hooks/AGENTS.md requires deterministic validation and independent review/challenge; the plan records both as required. Fixtures are synthetic (example.invalid). No contract file is loosened and no contract defect was found.
